title: Library-agnostic rayx: entry_dependencies, android_java_dirs, lockfile-seeded entry crates, graph-selected patches, project-or-default pins, a guard, the 1.x release policy and the 1.4.0 release

checks.descriptionMarkdown: New group `tests/pin_sources.rs`: project or default only, a workspace with a `gpux-testkit` member gets the defaults, declared Android pins come from the project, doctor shows two sources, files-only discovery.
The existing groups that encoded the gpux-checkout profile, rewritten to the generic rule (`project_pins`, `doctor`, `setup_android`).
New group `tests/app_entry_dependencies.rs`: `entry_dependencies` (sources, rename, target table, optional, default none, unlisted `rayx`/`rayx_devkit`, both errors) and generic feature forwarding.
New group `tests/app_entry_lockfile.rs`: all three entry crates seeded from the workspace lock, stale lock handling, the web dependency table without `zune-core`/`branches`.
New group `tests/app_entry_patches.rs`: patches selected by the feature-aware graph, written into all three entry crates with absolute paths, kept fields, quoted URL keys and valid TOML.
New named unit suite `app::android::devkit_contract_tests`: `--android-devkit` needs the app's `devkit` feature (checked before the toolchain), and the bridge message names no tool or package.
The existing descriptor and Playwright unit tests that encoded the removed couplings or the fixture's old crate names, rewritten to the generic form.
The existing group `tests/app_project.rs` after its entry-dependency and patch tests are rewritten to the generic form.

New named unit suite `app::wasm::package_fonts_tests`: fonts staged once from a package-asset declaration, absent in explicit mode without the id, nothing from an undeclared package named `gpux-fonts`.

The existing web, asset and package-asset unit tests after the font root is removed, the fixture's fonts package declares a package asset (and package assets use the shared graph), and the generated-page tests are rewritten for the app-owned page and the neutral fallback.
The existing group `tests/app_project.rs` after its `gpux-fonts` graph test is removed and the fixture's fonts package is renamed.

New group `tests/app_android_java_dirs.rs`: declarations collected from the app's feature-aware graph (app included), sorted and deduplicated, the joined property string, packages outside the graph ignored, each validation error.
New named unit suite `app::android::java_dirs_gradle_tests`: the Gradle build command carries `-PrayxAndroidJavaDirs=...` when directories are declared and no such property otherwise.

New group `tests/app_web_host_page.rs`: the app's `platform/web/index.html` copied with `__RAYX_MODULE__`, `__RAYX_TITLE__` and `__RAYX_DIAGNOSTICS__` replaced (diagnostics on and off, repeated placeholders, the rest unchanged), an unknown `__RAYX_*__` token refused with nothing written, and the neutral fallback page with none of the removed code.
New group `tests/library_agnostic.rs`: the scanner self-test, the repository scan of non-test `src/**/*.rs` with the allowlist (no stale entries), and the CLI's own `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`.
New group `tests/app_contract_docs.rs`: the contract page's keys, property, sections and absent names; README pin section; the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rule and their equality.

The existing groups that read the edited files: README sections (`readme_versions`), the package files (`package_layout`), `tests/dependency_sources.rs` after its module documentation points at the guard, and `release_automation` after the changelog body and `docs/releasing.md` change.

New group `tests/release_policy.rs`: `semver_check = false`, `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`, the changelog body renders `Migration` footers, and `docs/releasing.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` state the 1.x policy (no `feat!` advice left).
`cargo fmt --check` before each sprint checkpoint and push (CLAUDE.md iteration validation).

`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` before each sprint checkpoint and push: every test target still compiles after an item is deleted (for example `PinSource::GpuxCheckout`, `resolved_package_dir`), so the release PR's CI does not go red mid-epic.
`cargo fmt --check` for the package.

`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: compiles and lints the library, the binary and every test target, which also proves that no test group still names a deleted item (`PinSource::GpuxCheckout`, `GPUX_CHECKOUT`, `resolved_package_dir`, ...).

New named unit suite `app::android::devkit_graph_tests`: an `--android-devkit` build uses the selection plus `devkit` for the Android entry manifest (its `[patch]` entries) and package-asset staging, like the Java directories.

sprints.title: Pins from the project or the default: the gpux-checkout profile goes

tasks.title: Delete the gpux-checkout pin profile
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: In `src/project/pins.rs` remove `PinSource::GpuxCheckout`, `GpuxProfile`, `GPUX_CHECKOUT` and the `gpux` branch of the `pin` closure and of `android_build_tools`; update the module documentation (two sources) and reword the `DEFAULTS` comment so it names no library (it may keep pointing at the checklist `wasm-toolchain-update.md`). In `src/project/mod.rs` remove `Project::is_gpux_checkout`. Write `tests/pin_sources.rs` (temporary workspaces: one with a `gpux-testkit` member and no metadata, one declaring the three Android keys; files-only discovery with a failing recording runner as `tests/project_pins.rs` does; doctor text/JSON through the existing report API). Rewrite `tests/project_pins.rs` (`a_gpux_checkout_that_declares_nothing_uses_the_gpux_profile_for_android`, `project_metadata_beats_the_gpux_profile`, the files-only test's `gpux-checkout` case, the `GPUX_CHECKOUT` import), `tests/doctor.rs` (`pins_show_where_each_came_from`) and `tests/setup_android.rs` (three `PinSource::GpuxCheckout`), and delete `tests/fixtures/gpux-checkout/`. Commit as `feat(project): resolve pins from the project or the built-in defaults only` (no `!`, no `BREAKING CHANGE:`; 1.x policy), its body stating that the gpux-checkout profile is gone, with a `Migration:` footer naming the `[workspace.metadata.rayx]` keys that replace it. Before the sprint checkpoint: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`; after it, check that `git rev-list --count -E --grep='^[a-z]+(\([^)]*\))?!:' --grep='^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE:' v1.3.0..HEAD` prints 0 (1.x policy: no breaking markers), then `git push --force-with-lease origin main` (owner policy; no branch, no PR).

sprints.title: Generated entry crates: entry_dependencies, lockfile seeding, patches from the graph, the DevKit contract

tasks.title: entry_dependencies and generic feature forwarding
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Extend `project::Dependency` with `rename`, `target`, `features`, `default_features` from `cargo metadata` (`rename`, `target`, `features`, `uses_default_features`; best effort in the files-only `manifest_dependencies`), and `dependency_toml` to write `package`, `default-features = false`, `features` and `optional` beside the source. In `src/app/descriptor.rs` read `entry_dependencies`, resolve each key against the app package's normal dependency declarations (errors per ENTRY-1), write the declarations (target-specific ones under `[target.'<cfg>'.dependencies]`), and build feature lines generically (transitive walk per ENTRY-2, generalizing `manifest_has_active_dependency`). Delete `manifest_feature_contains`, the `devkit` special case, the `rayx`/`rayx_devkit` lines and their comment. Rewrite the `app-workspace` fixture: `crates/rayx` and `crates/rayx_devkit` become neutral packages (for example `crates/ui_runtime` and an optional `crates/inspector` behind an app feature such as `inspect = ["dep:inspector"]`), the fixture app lists them in `entry_dependencies`; update every reference to the old paths (`src/app/descriptor.rs`, `src/app/playwright.rs` and other unit tests, `tests/app_project.rs`, `tests/common` users). Write `tests/app_entry_dependencies.rs`. Commit as `feat(app): generated entry crates depend on the app's entry_dependencies`, its body stating the break (no implicit dependencies, no invented `devkit` feature), with a `Migration:` footer (list the crates `main.rs` uses in `entry_dependencies`).

tasks.title: Seed every entry crate from Cargo.lock; drop the zune-core and branches pins
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: In `write_generated_rust_manifest` copy the workspace `Cargo.lock` for every target (not only iOS), removing a stale lock first, and keep only `wasm-bindgen`/`wasm-bindgen-futures` in the web block (delete the `zune-core` and `branches` lines and the `rclite` comment). Rewrite the descriptor unit tests `the_ios_entry_crate_starts_from_the_workspace_lockfile` and `web_manifest_is_generated_with_the_locked_wasm_bindgen`. Write `tests/app_entry_lockfile.rs`. Commit as `feat(app): seed every generated entry crate from the project's Cargo.lock`, its body stating that the web entry crate no longer pins `zune-core` or adds `branches/std`, with a `Migration:` footer (the crate that needs `branches/std` declares it).

tasks.title: The app's resolved graph and root patches selected by it
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Create `src/app/graph.rs` per `d-app-graph` (cargo metadata through `host::Runner`, normal-edge walk from the app, packages with metadata) and move `package_assets::discover_package_assets` onto it (its tests in `app::package_assets` keep passing). Replace `generated_web_patch_lines` and `ProjectContext::root_patch_path` with the generic selection and TOML rendering of `d-entry-patches`, written into all three entry crates. Rewrite the fixture's `patches/indxdb` and `patches/rexie` as neutral crates.io patches: one reached through an optional app dependency behind a feature (for example `store = ["dep:store_backend"]`, `store_backend = { version = "0.1", optional = true }`), one never reached, and record the reached one (and the unused one as `[[patch.unused]]`) in the fixture's `Cargo.lock` next to the `wasm-bindgen` pin entry so `cargo metadata` never needs the crates.io index (checked during planning: with a complete lock, resolution is offline; without it Cargo updates the index). Rewrite `web_manifest_repeats_the_root_storage_patches_only_for_active_storage` (descriptor unit test) and `root_patches_come_from_the_selected_workspace` (`tests/app_project.rs`). Write `tests/app_entry_patches.rs`. Commit as `feat(app): repeat the root patches the app's graph uses in every entry crate`, its body stating the changed rule, with a `Migration:` footer if a project relied on the old gate.

tasks.title: --android-devkit needs the app's devkit feature; a generic registry hint
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: In `src/app/android.rs` check, in the build, run/deploy and pack entry points before `setup_android_machine`, that an `--android-devkit` build's app manifest defines a `devkit` feature (error per DEVKIT-1). Move the final bridge lines into a function returning the registration file and registry directory text without a command, tool or package name, and without "RayX DevKit" (DEVKIT-2); `install_android_devkit_bridge` prints it. Add the named suite `devkit_contract_tests` in `android.rs` (fixture app from `test_support::FixtureWorkspace` with and without the feature). Commit as `feat(app): --android-devkit requires the app's devkit feature` (body states the break; `Migration:` footer: define a `devkit` feature) and `fix(app): print only the DevKit registry location` (or one `feat(app)` commit covering both). Before the sprint checkpoint: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`; after it, check that `git rev-list --count -E --grep='^[a-z]+(\([^)]*\))?!:' --grep='^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE:' v1.3.0..HEAD` prints 0 (1.x policy: no breaking markers), then `git push --force-with-lease origin main` (owner policy; no branch, no PR).

sprints.title: Fonts as package assets, Android Java directories from the graph, and the app-owned web page

tasks.title: Delete the gpux-fonts extra root
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: In `src/app/wasm.rs` `copy_app_assets` stage through `assets::package_app_assets_with_selection` only; delete `assets::package_app_assets_with_additional_roots` (fold its body into the selection function) and `ProjectContext::{resolved_package_dir, find_resolved_package_dir}`. Rewrite the unit test `wasm_app_content_is_beside_index_and_outside_asset_catalog` (its font package declares a `kind = "fonts"` package asset and the app includes it) and add the named suite `package_fonts_tests` (FONT-1's three cases, temporary fixture packages as that test builds them). In the `app-workspace` fixture turn `crates/gpux_fonts` into a neutral fonts package (for example `crates/demo_fonts`, package `demo-fonts`) with `rayx.assets.toml` and `[package.metadata.rayx.assets]`, add its id to the fixture app's explicit `include`, and delete `the_gpux_fonts_assets_come_from_the_resolved_dependency_graph` from `tests/app_project.rs`; fix any asset expectation the new package changes in `app::assets`/`app::package_assets`. Commit as `feat(app): fonts come only through package assets`, its body stating the break, with a `Migration:` footer (a fonts package declares a package asset; explicit-mode apps add its id to `include`).

tasks.title: android_java_dirs and -PrayxAndroidJavaDirs
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add `AppDescriptor::android_java_dirs` and the public property helper per `d-android-java-dirs` (re-exported from `rayx_cli::app` like `wasm_cargo_command`), compute the directories before Gradle in `build_android_app_with_toolchain` and pass them through `apply_android_gradle_properties`. Add fixture declarations (for example a `java/` directory with one placeholder file in the neutral runtime package, one in the optional package behind its feature, one in a workspace member the app does not depend on). Write `tests/app_android_java_dirs.rs` and the named suite `java_dirs_gradle_tests` in `android.rs`. Commit as `feat(app): pass the Android Java directories packages declare to Gradle`.

tasks.title: The app-owned platform/web/index.html and a neutral fallback page
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Per WEB-1, WEB-2 and `d-web-host-page` (amendment 2): add `AppDescriptor::web_page()`, replace `write_wasm_host` with the page function (app page or embedded neutral fallback; the three placeholders; unknown `__RAYX_<NAME>__` tokens refused with token, path and line), render it before `cargo build` in `build_with_profile` and write it where the host page is written today; re-export it from `rayx_cli::app`. Delete `html_island_diagnostics_bootstrap` and every `__DIAGNOSTIC_*__`/`__HTML_ISLAND_DIAGNOSTICS__` substitution. Rewrite the `app::wasm` unit tests that assert the removed page code (delete `html_island_diagnostics_bootstrap_includes_probe_contract`; `all_features_selects_a_diagnostics_enabled_wasm_host` and `generated_wasm_host_diagnostics_policy_omits_diagnostics_for_production` assert the `__RAYX_DIAGNOSTICS__` value; the base-href and deep-link tests use the fallback). `tests/app_wasm_fixture.rs` (ignored, web set) keeps passing unchanged: the fallback still names `/threaded_wasm_app_web.js`. Write `tests/app_web_host_page.rs`. Commit as `feat(app): the web page is the app's platform/web/index.html`, its body stating that `rayx` no longer generates diagnostics, HTML-island, thread or WebGPU code, with a `Migration:` footer (an app that relied on the generated diagnostics page adds `platform/web/index.html` using `__RAYX_MODULE__`, `__RAYX_TITLE__`, `__RAYX_DIAGNOSTICS__`). Before the sprint checkpoint: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`; after it, check that `git rev-list --count -E --grep='^[a-z]+(\([^)]*\))?!:' --grep='^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE:' v1.3.0..HEAD` prints 0 (1.x policy: no breaking markers), then `git push --force-with-lease origin main` (owner policy; no branch, no PR).

tasks.title: The 1.x release policy: Migration footers in the changelog, docs/releasing.md, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Per POL-1 and `d-release-1x`: add a `commit.footers` loop to the `[changelog] body` of `release-plz.toml` that prints `Migration` footers under the commit line (nothing else in `release-plz.toml` changes; `semver_check = false` and `release_commits` stay). Rewrite the commit table and the breaking-change advice of `docs/releasing.md` into the 1.x policy, and add the short Releases paragraph to `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (identical). Write `tests/release_policy.rs`. Commit as `docs(release): stay on 1.x and carry migration notes in Migration footers` (the template change may be its own `build(release): ...` commit). Before the sprint checkpoint: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`; after it, check that `git rev-list --count -E --grep='^[a-z]+(\([^)]*\))?!:' --grep='^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE:' v1.3.0..HEAD` prints 0 (1.x policy: no breaking markers), then `git push --force-with-lease origin main` (owner policy; no branch, no PR).

sprints.title: Release rayx 1.4.0 (GitHub-dependent; blanket go-ahead) and install it on this Mac

tasks.title: Local release-plz preview, everything on main, the release PR proposes 1.4.0
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: POL-2: install release-plz on this Mac if missing (for example `cargo binstall release-plz` or `brew install release-plz`), `git fetch origin --tags`, create a throwaway `git worktree` of the local `main`, run `release-plz update` there, read the proposed version (`1.4.0`) and the new `CHANGELOG.md` section (the `Migration:` notes rendered, no `[**breaking**]`), then remove the worktree; nothing is committed from it. REL-1: make sure every epic commit is on `origin/main` (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, the pre-push count of `PUSH` prints 0, `git push --force-with-lease origin main`). Wait for the Release-plz run on `main` and read the release PR (`gh pr list --repo rayx-ui/RayX.CLI`, `gh pr view <n> --json title,files`): version `1.4.0`, only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md` changed, the `Migration:` notes in the section. A 2.x proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`: keep a local ref at the current head (so checkpointed commits stay reachable), reword that commit, force-push with `--force-with-lease`, and re-read; never merge a 2.x PR. Record POL-2 and REL-1 in `docs/manual-verification.md` and commit as `docs(verify): ...`.

tasks.title: Merge the release PR under the blanket go-ahead; tag v1.4.0 and the GitHub Release
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: The owner pre-approved the merge (amendment 1, D): no stop to ask, but merge only when the release PR's CI and Release-build runs are green (a red run goes through the repair loop first), its version is still `1.4.0` and it changes only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`. `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` exists (amendment 1, C); if a release-plz run fails at checkout or push, report it to the owner instead of retrying blindly. Then watch release-plz push `v1.4.0` and the dist Release workflow finish (`gh run list`, `gh run watch`), check `gh release view v1.4.0 --repo rayx-ui/RayX.CLI`, fast-forward the local `main`, and record REL-2 in `docs/manual-verification.md`.

tasks.title: rayx self update --release 1.4.0 on this Mac
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Run `rayx self update --release 1.4.0`, `rayx --version`, and `rayx doctor --json` in a workspace without `[workspace.metadata.rayx]` (pin sources `project`/`default` only). The owner accepted (amendment 1, D) that local RayX app builds use `rayx self update --release 1.3.0` until RayX's `rayx-released-libraries` switch; note that in the record. Record REL-3 in `docs/manual-verification.md`, commit as `docs(verify): ...`, fetch/rebase and push.

sprints.title: Final-review repair: one feature selection for a devkit Android build

tasks.title: Build the devkit Android graph from one selection
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Final review finding F-FINAL-DEVKIT-GRAPH: `build_android_app_with_toolchain` collected the Java directories with the selection plus `devkit` but generated the Android entry manifest (and so its graph-selected `[patch]` entries) and staged package assets with the plain selection. Compute `built_feature_selection(features, options)` once and use it for all three; the cargo-ndk arguments stay unchanged. Add the named unit suite `app::android::devkit_graph_tests` (a patch and an asset package reached only through the app's `devkit` feature appear only in a devkit build). Commit as `fix(app): build the --android-devkit graph from the selection plus devkit`; it ships in the next 1.x patch release (the release PR is left open for the owner).
